abstract: Maintains wide-area terrestrial backhaul paths, carrier routing diversities, and X-band baseband ingestion records
system_message:
You are Telecommunications network lead (NET). The Telecommunications network lead (NET) is responsible for maintaining wide-area terrestrial backhaul paths, carrier routing diversities, and X-band baseband ingestion records across ground station proposals, as well as tracking network transit latency records.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Network transit latency（LATENCY）
information_points.content:
NET-LATENCY-D6G：For the Mid-latitude dual-reflector earth station, the core pop round-trip latency from the station gateway to the regional mission operations center is 28 ms.
NET-LATENCY-18O：For the Equatorial high-elevation tracking complex, the core pop round-trip latency from the station gateway to the regional mission operations center is 18 ms.
NET-LATENCY-1DP：For the Polar orbit dedicated tracking facility, the core pop round-trip latency from the station gateway to the regional mission operations center is 38 ms.

information_points.title: Maintains wide-area terrestrial backhaul paths, carrier routing diversities, and X-band baseband ingestion records（BACKHAUL）
information_points.content:
NET-BACKHAUL-1ZR：For the Polar orbit dedicated tracking facility, dual-homed fiber backhaul redundancy via two geographically diverse routing paths at the station demarcation point is true, and the primary X-band carrier ingestion throughput delivered to network buffers is 9.0 Gbps.
NET-BACKHAUL-22Q：For the Equatorial high-elevation tracking complex, dual-homed fiber backhaul redundancy via two geographically diverse routing paths at the station demarcation point is false, and the primary X-band carrier ingestion throughput delivered to network buffers is 4.5 Gbps.
NET-BACKHAUL-GE6：For the Mid-latitude dual-reflector earth station, dual-homed fiber backhaul redundancy via two geographically diverse routing paths at the station demarcation point is true, and the primary X-band carrier ingestion throughput delivered to network buffers is 9.0 Gbps.
